episodes.name: Gujjar quota agitation
episodes.summary: Police fired on protesters blocking roads and railway lines for Scheduled Tribe status, at Bayana and Sikandra; the agitation spread across eastern Rajasthan.

deaths.quote: eatures Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up News India caste riot toll rises Violent protests by Gujjar community have left 37 people dead in Rajasthan state.

episodes.name: Kandhamal violence
episodes.summary: Attacks on Christians after the killing of a Hindu leader; houses and churches burned across the district.

deaths.quote: Government figures put the death toll at 38.

disputes: Local monitoring groups put deaths at 90 or more and estimate 5,600 houses and 300 churches and places of worship destroyed (CSW).

episodes.name: Bodo–Muslim clashes in lower Assam
episodes.summary: Clashes between Bodos and Muslim settlers in Kokrajhar, Chirang and Dhubri; one of India's largest displacements of the period.

deaths.quote: ps Prefer on Google W Wasbir Hussain Updated on: 17 January 2024 3:05 pm Published at: 30 July 2012 12:00 am A Turf War A riot, clearly a battle over living space, between ethnic Bodo tribes-people and Muslim settlers, cohabiting for decades in western Assam, has left 57 confirmed dead, six of them in police firing, and more than 400,000 displaced from their homes in a week-long rampage, beginning July 21, 2012.

displaced.quote: 24 3:05 pm Published at: 30 July 2012 12:00 am A Turf War A riot, clearly a battle over living space, between ethnic Bodo tribes-people and Muslim settlers, cohabiting for decades in western Assam, has left 57 confirmed dead, six of them in police firing, and more than 400,000 displaced from their homes in a week-long rampage, beginning July 21, 2012.

disputes: An early count: Outlook, 30 July 2012, ten days into the violence. Of the 57, six died in police firing.

episodes.name: Muzaffarnagar and Shamli riots
episodes.summary: Communal violence in western Uttar Pradesh in August–September 2013; tens of thousands fled to relief camps.

deaths.quote: Officially, the killing spree that went on for weeks took 64 lives in Shamli, Muzaffarnagar and adjacent districts.
deaths.who: official count, as reviewed by Maktoob

displaced.quote: About 60,000 people, almost all Muslims, took refuge in camps near Muslim-dominated settlements due to violence in their native villages.

episodes.name: Patidar quota agitation
episodes.summary: Violence after a rally in Ahmedabad demanding OBC status for Patidars; curfew in several cities and the army deployed.

disputes: The Quint counts 14 people who died during the agitation between 2015 and 2017.

episodes.name: Jat quota agitation
episodes.summary: Roads and railways blockaded, police stations attacked and shops, schools and vehicles burned across Rohtak and neighbouring districts. The Prakash Singh committee found "twenty rioters and ten others were killed".

injured.quote: Twenty rioters and ten others were killed, while 208 persons (including 70 security personnel) were injured.

policeInjured.quote: Twenty rioters and ten others were killed, while 208 persons (including 70 security personnel) were injured.

firs.quote: More than 1,500 criminal cases were registered, mainly of theft, arson, mischief and robbery.

disputes: The committee recorded about 2,000 shops set ablaze, 371 vehicles damaged or burned, and arson in 30 schools and colleges.

episodes.name: Violence after the Dera Sacha Sauda verdict
episodes.summary: Followers of Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh rioted in Panchkula and elsewhere after his conviction for rape; the High Court ordered Dera property attached to pay for the damage.

deaths.quote: enced to 20 years in prison by a special CBI court for raping two female followers, the Haryana government has sent a detailed report to the Centre on the recent events involving his court appearance and the violence in Panchkula that followed his conviction, which left 38 dead and hundreds injured.
deaths.who: Haryana government report to the Centre

episodes.name: Bharat Bandh against the SC/ST Act ruling
episodes.summary: Dalit organisations' nationwide shutdown against a Supreme Court ruling on arrests under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act; deaths in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.

episodes.summary: Stations, trains and tracks attacked across West Bengal from 13 to 15 December 2019 during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act.

episodes.summary: Protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act turned violent across the state on 20–21 December; the state issued recovery notices for damage, later withdrawn before the Supreme Court.

episodes.name: North-east Delhi riots
episodes.summary: Communal violence between 23 and 26 February 2020 between supporters and opponents of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act.

deaths.quote: The violence claimed 53 lives and hundreds were injured.

disputes: The Delhi Police list of the dead names 52 civilians and one policeman, head constable Ratan Lal (The Wire).
Of 541 FIRs for damage to property, 23 concerned public property and 518 private property (Delhi Police affidavit).

episodes.summary: A mob attacked two police stations in Bengaluru over a social media post; police opened fire.

episodes.name: Protests against the Agnipath scheme
episodes.summary: Protests against the new military recruitment scheme; trains and stations attacked and set on fire. 2,132 trains were cancelled between 15 and 23 June.
